title: India vs Pakistan at Asian Games 2026 Possible Only in Final or Bronze Match
excerpt: The official draw for the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games places cricket rivals India and Pakistan on opposite sides of the knockout bracket, meaning the two teams can only meet if both reach the semi-finals or later.
body:
• India and Pakistan have been placed on opposite sides of the mens cricket knockout bracket at the 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan.
  • An India-Pakistan clash is possible only in the gold medal final or the bronze medal playoff — not before the semi-finals.
  • Both nations have received direct quarter-final berths along with Sri Lanka and Bangladesh, based on ICC T20I rankings.
  • India enter as defending champions in both the mens and womens competitions after sweeping gold at the 2023 Hangzhou Games.

Draw Keeps Rivals Apart

Cricket fans hoping for an early India-Pakistan showdown at the 2026 Asian Games will have to wait. The official tournament draw, announced by the Olympic Council of Asia, has placed the two heavyweight cricketing nations on completely opposite sides of the mens knockout bracket.

The only scenarios in which India and Pakistan will face each other: both teams win their respective quarter-final and semi-final matches to set up a gold medal final, or both suffer unexpected semi-final defeats and meet in the bronze medal playoff.

The 10-team mens competition will be played in the T20 International format at Korogi Athletic Park in Aichi Prefecture, with all matches carrying full international status. The tournament runs from September 24 to October 1.

Top Four Seeds Get Direct Entry

Based on ICC T20I rankings, India, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, and Bangladesh have received direct entry into the quarter-finals, bypassing the preliminary round. The remaining six teams are divided into two groups to compete for the final four knockout berths.

Group A features Afghanistan, Japan, and Nepal, while Group B comprises Hong Kong China, Malaysia, and Oman. The top two teams from each group will advance to join the seeded nations in the quarter-finals.

India will face one of the qualifying teams in the last eight. Shreyas Iyer will captain the mens side, with Tilak Varma serving as vice-captain. The squad also includes teenage batting sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, who recently made his mark in international cricket with a historic half-century against Zimbabwe.

Womens Draw Also Keeps Rivals Separated

The womens cricket competition, running from September 17 to 22, features an eight-team direct knockout format. India will open their title defence against hosts Japan in the quarter-finals.

"India enter the 2026 Asian Games as defending champions in both competitions after winning gold medals in Hangzhou in 2023."

— Reuters

If Harmanpreet Kaurs side advance, they would face either Bangladesh or China in the semi-finals. Pakistan are on the other side of the womens draw, meeting Thailand in their quarter-final, with Sri Lanka or Malaysia awaiting the winner.

An India-Pakistan womens clash is therefore also only possible in the final.

India Defending Double Gold

India enter the tournament as reigning champions in both the mens and womens events. The mens team claimed gold at the 2023 Hangzhou Games under Ruturaj Gaikwad, beating Afghanistan in a rain-affected final on superior seeding. Harmanpreet Kaur led the womens team to gold by defending 116 against Sri Lanka, with Titas Sadhu taking three wickets for six runs.

Cricket is returning to the Asian Games for the fourth time, after Guangzhou 2010, Incheon 2014, and Hangzhou 2023. The format provides a rare opportunity for Asian nations to compete for medals in the sport on the continental stage.

For the Indian diaspora, an India-Pakistan final at the Asian Games would rank among the most-watched sporting events of the year — but both teams will first need to navigate their respective paths through the bracket.
